title: Parabolic Long
teaches: The parabolic long as we trade it: Bracco's parabolic burst mirrored, a 3 to 5 day accelerating panic drop that ends on a gap-down climax day, bought only after the turn on the first 5-minute close back over VWAP, the stop a few cents under the climax low, the daily 9 EMA as the target, the one long our 200-day rule allows below the line, and a loss taken at the stop as the cost of being a day early.

facts.claim: Kullamagi: the long comes after a successful parabolic short falls 50-60% or more in a few days.

facts.quote: Entry is opening range highs or the first green 5-minute candle or any range break to the upside if the stock doesn’t rally out of the gate, which they usually do.
facts.claim: Kullamagi's entry: the opening-range high, the first green 5-minute candle or a range break up.

facts.quote: This is by far the riskiest setup if done wrong or if you have issues with not obeying your stops.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: by far the riskiest setup if done wrong or if stops are not obeyed.

facts.quote: Think of stocks as rubber bands, if they get really stretched short term, they can have powerful snapbacks.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: stocks stretched short term snap back like rubber bands.

facts.quote: These things can bounce 50-100% in a few days.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the bounce can be 50% to 100% in a few days.

facts.quote: Don’t be too early. WAIT for the right setup. Let the amateur shorts get run over, that’s where your edge comes in.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: do not be too early; wait for the right setup.

facts.quote: Most of these are short setups, but sometimes there are also good long setups but they don’t occur as often.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the long version is rarer than the short.

facts.quote: That's when price plunges in a straight line drop, day after day, with little or no overlap between price bars.

facts.claim: O'Neil: stocks that fall more than normal are under heavy liquidation for a reason.

questions.q: In one line, what is a parabolic long?
choices: The turn after a 3 to 5 day drop
Riding a stock up its run
A breakout from a quiet base
A bottom built slowly over months
questions.answer: The turn after a 3 to 5 day drop
questions.why: The turn after a 3 to 5 day panic drop. Bracco's burst turned upside down: a stock falls straight down for days, then snaps back.
questions.lesson_line: A parabolic long buys the snap back, not the fall.

wrong.Riding a stock up its run: That is buying the run up, the opposite trade. Ours is the mirror of a burst down.
wrong.A breakout from a quiet base: A base is a rest. This setup has no rest; it is a panic and a turn.
wrong.A bottom built slowly over months: Months of basing is a different trade. This bounce lives for days.

questions.q: Our parabolic long is Bracco's parabolic burst mirrored: three straight down days, two gap downs, rising volume.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Our rulebook makes the long the mirror image of Bracco's burst. Three straight lower closes, two gap-down opens, bigger losses, rising volume, a climax gap down.
questions.lesson_line: Read Bracco's burst upside down. That is our parabolic long.

questions.q: What is the target of a parabolic long, and whose rule is it?
choices: The daily 9 EMA, Bracco's rule
The 50-day average, from below
The high before the fall began
A fixed 20% bounce off the low
questions.answer: The daily 9 EMA, Bracco's rule
questions.why: The daily 9 EMA from below. Bracco's parabolic short targets the 9 EMA; the rulebook keeps it and the long mirrors it.
questions.lesson_line: The 9 EMA is the finish line. The trade is done when price gets there.

wrong.The 50-day average, from below: After a crash the 50-day is far above. The 9 EMA is the first average price can reach.
wrong.The high before the fall began: A snap back is not a round trip. The old high is not the plan.
wrong.A fixed 20% bounce off the low: Bracco targets an average, not a percent. The 9 EMA moves with the stock.

questions.q: Which is the one long our 200-day rule allows below the line?
choices: A parabolic long
A flat base breakout
Any stock down 30%
A pullback to the 50-day
questions.answer: A parabolic long
questions.why: A parabolic long. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. A hard rule with one exception.
questions.lesson_line: Below the 200-day there is one long, and this is it.

wrong.A flat base breakout: A flat base needs price above the 200-day. No exception.
wrong.Any stock down 30%: A percent fall is not the exception. The parabolic burst is.
wrong.A pullback to the 50-day: A pullback long needs the lines in order. Below the 200-day it is off.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: On the main version the buy day is the ___ day, the gap-down day.
questions.answer: climax
questions.why: The climax day. The gap-down day at the end of the burst is the day the long is bought, after the turn.
questions.lesson_line: The buy day is the climax day. Not the day before, and not a week later.

questions.q: A parabolic long needs an RS rating of 80 or more, like the other longs we buy.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The leader rule exempts parabolic and mean-reversion trades. The burst is the test here, not the rating.
questions.lesson_line: RS does not apply here. The burst is the whole story.

questions.q: The VWAP reclaim fills you. Bracco's short takes a second entry later. Our long?
choices: One entry; full size at one price
A second buy over the day's high
Add on every new high
Half now, half at the 9 EMA
questions.answer: One entry; full size at one price
questions.why: One entry. The full size at one price with one stop; no adding. Bracco's second entry is his; our rulebook settled it.
questions.lesson_line: One price, one stop, one trade. The second entry is not ours.

wrong.A second buy over the day's high: That is the mirror of Bracco's short add. Our rule is one entry.
wrong.Add on every new high: Adding is not in the rulebook. Full size at one price.
wrong.Half now, half at the 9 EMA: The 9 EMA is where the trade ends, not where it grows.

questions.q: On the climax day, when exactly is the buy?
choices: First 5-minute close over VWAP
The open, before any turn shows
The close, whatever the day did
A buy stop over the prior high
questions.answer: First 5-minute close over VWAP
questions.why: The first 5-minute close back above VWAP, after the low is in. Never before the turn. Bracco's short waits for the break under VWAP; the long waits for the reclaim.
questions.lesson_line: The right side of the V. VWAP reclaimed, after the low, is the buy.

wrong.The open, before any turn shows: That is buying the knife. The turn has not happened at the open.
wrong.The close, whatever the day did: The close is a scanner's stand-in. The real buy is the intraday reclaim, usually lower.
wrong.A buy stop over the prior high: Too far away. The prior day's high is a whole gap above.

questions.q: On the climax-day entry the stop sits a few cents under the climax day's low.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A few cents under the day's low, not exactly on it. Bracco's short exits if the day's high is reclaimed; the mirror is the day's low.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the climax low.

questions.q: By Bracco's post mirrored, how long is the burst down?
choices: 3 to 5 sessions
One day
Two to three weeks
A month or more
questions.answer: 3 to 5 sessions
questions.why: 3 to 5 sessions. The burst is the final leg, and the climax gap usually comes on day 3 to 5 of the move.
questions.lesson_line: Three to five days of panic, then the climax. Longer is a decline, not a burst.

wrong.One day: A one-day flush in a leader is Mean Reversion, not this card.
wrong.Two to three weeks: The decline before the burst can run weeks. The burst itself is days.
wrong.A month or more: A month down is a grind. The burst is the accelerating end.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The climax day ends at ___ times its 50-day average volume or more.
questions.why: 2 times. The climax day ends at 2 times its 50-day average volume or more, with volume rising through the burst. Bracco's box: two days of rising volume.
questions.lesson_line: A climax without a crowd is not a climax. Two times average, rising.

questions.q: A close under the lower Bollinger band the day before is the trigger to buy.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A close under the lower band is a plus, not a trigger. The trigger is the VWAP reclaim on the climax day.
questions.lesson_line: Outside the Bollinger band says stretched. It does not say buy.

questions.q: Which decline is parabolic?
choices: Each leg steeper, bars barely overlap
A stair-step, every dip bought
A slow drift under the 50-day
A flat range for weeks
questions.answer: Each leg steeper, bars barely overlap
questions.why: Each leg steeper, little bar overlap. An orderly, overlapping decline is not this setup. Bulkowski's vertical run down: a straight-line drop, day after day.
questions.lesson_line: Parabolic means accelerating. A stair-step is a different animal.

wrong.A stair-step, every dip bought: A stair-step is orderly. There is no panic to snap back from.
wrong.A slow drift under the 50-day: A drift is a grind. No range expansion, no climax.
wrong.A flat range for weeks: A range is a base. Nothing is falling.

questions.q: Parabolic long candidate?
questions.story: A stock broke a three-month support level yesterday for the first time. Today is its second straight down day. It closes near its low on heavy volume.
choices: No; day two of a breakdown is too early
Yes; heavy volume means capitulation
Yes, if it reclaims VWAP tomorrow
questions.answer: No; day two of a breakdown is too early
questions.why: No. The first or second day of a breakdown from a top is not this setup. Bracco passed on exactly this: a second down day and the first break of support.
questions.lesson_line: Day two of a breakdown is the start of the fall, not the end.

wrong.Yes; heavy volume means capitulation: Heavy volume on day two is the selling starting, not finishing.
wrong.Yes, if it reclaims VWAP tomorrow: A reclaim needs a burst behind it. Two days is not a burst.

questions.q: No new parabolic long in the 3 sessions before the company's earnings report.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. A crash into a report is a gap you cannot stop.
questions.lesson_line: The calendar comes before the chart. Three sessions before a report, no buy.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five mirrored boxes?
choices: A close under the 200-day
Three straight lower closes
Two straight gap-down opens
A gap down on the climax day
questions.answer: A close under the 200-day
questions.why: A close under the 200-day is not a box. The five: three lower closes, two gap-down opens, two of three days losing more. Then two days of rising volume and a climax gap down.
questions.lesson_line: Count the five boxes. The 200-day is a separate rule, not a box.

wrong.Three straight lower closes: Box one. Bracco's three straight days of gains, mirrored.
wrong.Two straight gap-down opens: Box two. The climax day may be the second gap.
wrong.A gap down on the climax day: Box five. Bracco will not short without the climax gap.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You bought the VWAP reclaim at 41.20 with the stop a few cents under the day's low. At 1:30 it loses VWAP and prints a new low of the day.
choices: Out; the stop under the low is hit
Hold; give it room until the close
Add; it is cheaper than the fill
Move the stop under the week's low
questions.answer: Out; the stop under the low is hit
questions.why: Out. The entry bar failed back under VWAP and the day's low broke. The stop under the day's low is the exit, and a new low means the selling was not done.
questions.lesson_line: Lose VWAP and the low, and the thesis is wrong. The stop says so first.

wrong.Hold; give it room until the close: The stop does not wait for the close. A new low of the day is the exit.
wrong.Add; it is cheaper than the fill: Never add when down. Full size at one price.
wrong.Move the stop under the week's low: The stop only moves up, never wider.

questions.q: The trigger prints at 20.00. Three minutes later it trades 21.00. Buy?
choices: No; 5% over, past our 4% line
Yes; momentum confirms it
Yes, at half size, lower risk
Yes, with the stop raised
questions.answer: No; 5% over, past our 4% line
questions.why: No. 21.00 is 5% over the trigger and our line is 4%. Chasing costs size: the stop stays put, the distance grows, the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: A snap back moves fast. Past 4% over the trigger, let it go.

wrong.Yes; momentum confirms it: Confirmed and too far away are both true. The chase line is 4%.
wrong.Yes, at half size, lower risk: Half of a chased entry is still chased.
wrong.Yes, with the stop raised: The stop is the day's low. Raising it to fit a late entry is the mistake.

questions.q: The 50-day is 180.00, ATR 4.00, the close before the climax day 150.00. How many ATR under the 50-day is it?
questions.why: 7.5 ATR. The 50-day minus the close, divided by the ATR. Bracco looks for range and volume expansion; the ATR stretch tells you how far price has run.
questions.lesson_line: Stretch is measured in ATRs under the 50-day. Do the division.

questions.q: The stop on a parabolic long can wait in your head, since the trade lasts just days.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Every position has a real stop order with the broker. After a crash, gaps are common; a stop in your head cannot catch one.
questions.lesson_line: A stop in your head is a debate. Put it with the broker.

questions.q: When is the parabolic long at its best?
choices: When the index is capitulating too
In a calm, rising market
On day one of a breakdown
When one stock falls alone
questions.answer: When the index is capitulating too
questions.why: When the index is capitulating too: a stretched index, a gap down, a Monday, a VIX spike. Kell says the same: get aggressive when the index prints the reversal.
questions.lesson_line: One stock crashing is a story. The whole market crashing is a setup.

wrong.In a calm, rising market: A calm market has no panic to reverse. This is a fear trade.
wrong.On day one of a breakdown: Day one is the start of the fall. The burst comes later.
wrong.When one stock falls alone: A lone crash is often the company's own news. The best turns are market-wide.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The trade is done when price reaches the daily ___ EMA from below.
questions.why: The 9 EMA. Bracco's studies make the 9 EMA the magnet; our rulebook keeps it as the parabolic target.
questions.lesson_line: Nine. The daily 9 EMA from below is where this trade ends.

questions.q: Buy the close, or wait?
questions.story: It is Friday. The index is four down days deep and stretched under its 50-day. The VIX is 28. A liquid ETF has three boxes and a green close.
choices: Wait; Monday may bring the real flush
Buy the close; the turn is in
Buy half now, add Monday
Short it into Monday
questions.answer: Wait; Monday may bring the real flush
questions.why: Wait. Do not buy the Friday before a possible Monday flush; Bracco's best turns come on Mondays. Three of the four stopped-out examples we studied (BAC, WDC, KRE) were Friday buys.
questions.lesson_line: Friday's turn is often Monday's gap. Let the weekend decide.

wrong.Buy the close; the turn is in: A Friday close is the worst place to find out. The Monday gap goes through every stop.
wrong.Buy half now, add Monday: Half of a Friday buy still eats the gap. One entry, on the turn.
wrong.Short it into Monday: Four days down and stretched is not where we short. Cash, then watch Monday.

questions.q: On one name you may never try a parabolic long more than 3 times in a week and 6 in a month.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. At most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month, each on a new trigger. After three tries the name is telling you something.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week. After that the name is telling you something.

questions.q: The peak four sessions ago was 88.00 and today's low is 50.00. How far has it fallen, in percent?
questions.why: 43.2%. The peak minus the low, divided by the peak. Kullamagi's premise for the long is a parabolic short that fell 50-60% or more in a few days.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the fall from the peak to the climax low. Percent, then structure.

questions.q: Entry 20.50, stop 19.80, the 9 EMA at 21.70. How many R to the 9 EMA?
questions.why: 1.7R. The 9 EMA minus the entry, divided by the entry minus the stop. Our card wants the 9 EMA at least 2R above the entry; here there is no room.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the room to the 9 EMA before you buy. Under 2R, pass.

questions.q: Where is the stop now?
questions.story: You bought at 30.00 with the stop at 29.00. Next morning it opens 28.70, under the stop. The first 30-minute bar's low is 28.50.
choices: 28.50, the first 30-minute low
Sell at the open, 28.70
No stop until it reclaims 29.00
Out; the gap is past 2R
questions.answer: 28.50, the first 30-minute low
questions.why: 28.50. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low. That low is a loss inside the 2R ceiling, so it is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the one exception. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Sell at the open, 28.70: The gap rule gives it 30 minutes. The open is not the decision.
wrong.No stop until it reclaims 29.00: There is always a stop. The new one is the 30-minute low.
wrong.Out; the gap is past 2R: The loss at the 30-minute low is inside the 2R ceiling.

questions.q: Add here?
questions.story: Your parabolic long is down 1.5% from the fill, still above the stop. A friend says buy more here; the average improves.
choices: No; one price, one stop, no adds
Yes; the lower average is a plus
Yes, a small add is fine here
Yes, and move the stop lower
questions.answer: No; one price, one stop, no adds
questions.why: No. The full size at one price with one stop; no adding. Bracco: I never add when I am down. The stop is the only plan for a loser.
questions.lesson_line: A lower average on a loser is a bigger loser. Never add down.

wrong.Yes; the lower average is a plus: A better average on a losing thesis is more risk, not a better trade.
wrong.Yes, a small add is fine here: Small is still adding. The rule is one price.
wrong.Yes, and move the stop lower: The stop never moves wider. Two mistakes in one.

questions.q: The climax day's low sits 7.3% under your fill. What now?
choices: Size down; between 3% and 8%
Skip; over 3% is never traded
Full size; the stop is the stop
Tighten the stop to 3%
questions.answer: Size down; between 3% and 8%
questions.why: Size down by the formula. Between 3% and 8% the honest stop stays and the shares shrink; over 8%, skip. AGQ's stop was 7.3% and it still paid.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last. A wide honest stop means fewer shares.

wrong.Skip; over 3% is never traded: Three percent is where the stop usually sits, not a wall. The skip line here is 8%.
wrong.Full size; the stop is the stop: Full size with a 7.3% stop breaks the risk budget. The size comes from the stop.
wrong.Tighten the stop to 3%: A stop pulled inside the noise is not a stop. Never pull it in to fit the size.

questions.q: Our card moves the parabolic long's stop to breakeven at 2R, the low end of the house window.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Breakeven at 2R, the low end of the 2R to 5R window, because the bounce is short.
questions.lesson_line: Two R and the stop goes to the fill. The bounce does not wait for you.

questions.q: Buy now?
questions.story: The climax day gaps down 6% and keeps sliding at 10:00. It is 45% off its peak with every box ticked. Every tick looks cheaper.
choices: No; never before the turn
Yes; every box is ticked
Yes; the gap is the buy signal
Yes, a starter now, more at VWAP
questions.answer: No; never before the turn
questions.why: No. Never before the turn: the buy is the first 5-minute close back over VWAP after the low. Buying the gap or the low first is buying the knife.
questions.lesson_line: Cheap is not a trigger. The reclaim is.

wrong.Yes; every box is ticked: The boxes say it is a candidate. The turn says it is a trade. Not yet.
wrong.Yes; the gap is the buy signal: The gap is box five. The signal is the VWAP reclaim after the low.
wrong.Yes, a starter now, more at VWAP: A starter before the turn is a knife with a smaller handle. One entry, at the reclaim.

questions.q: On the climax day, how do the opening minutes compare with the other burst days?
choices: The heaviest opening of the run
The lightest; sellers are tired
About the same as the other days
Heavy only if the gap filled
questions.answer: The heaviest opening of the run
questions.why: The heaviest of the run. Bracco: the climax day almost invariably shows the highest opening volume of the entire run. The long reads it mirrored.
questions.lesson_line: The climax opens with the loudest crowd of the whole move.

wrong.The lightest; sellers are tired: Tired sellers come later. The climax is the panic, the heaviest selling.
wrong.About the same as the other days: A climax that looks like any day is not a climax.
wrong.Heavy only if the gap filled: The opening volume comes with the gap, filled or not.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: After the entry, a trade under the ___ low means the selling was not done.
questions.answer: climax
questions.why: The climax low. A trade under it is the stop; the Wyckoff school reads a lower test as new lows or a long consolidation.
questions.lesson_line: A new low under the climax says the panic is not finished. The stop agrees.

questions.q: Was the stop the mistake?
questions.story: Every box ticked: a 3.9% gap down, 3.6x volume, a close 1.8% off the open, 6.2 ATR under the 50-day. You bought at 28.50, stop 27.67. Monday's low of 27.44 took it; the stock traded 17.95 three weeks later.
choices: No; a planned loss, as designed
Yes; the stop needed more room
Yes; the wrong boxes were ticked
No; sell at the close instead
questions.answer: No; a planned loss, as designed
questions.why: No. The stop is the exit and it kept the cost to one R. It was the first week of a crash from an all-time high; the bars cannot show that, the market reading has to.
questions.lesson_line: The stop keeps a week-early call at one R. That is what it is for.

wrong.Yes; the stop needed more room: Room would have been a 37% hole. The stop saved most of it.
wrong.Yes; the wrong boxes were ticked: Every box was ticked. The problem was where in the crash the day sat.
wrong.No; sell at the close instead: A stop with the broker, not a close you had to watch. The stop did the job.

questions.q: Same climax, two names: both tick all five boxes. For one the index is capitulating too; for the other it is calm. Grade?
choices: The first grades higher
Equal; the boxes decide
The second; a calm index is safer
questions.answer: The first grades higher
questions.why: The first. An index capitulating too makes the stronger case; a calm index or one only starting to break down weakens it. Same boxes, different grade.
questions.lesson_line: Grade the market with the stock. A calm index drops the grade.

wrong.Equal; the boxes decide: The boxes are the pattern. The market is the context, and it grades.
wrong.The second; a calm index is safer: A calm index means a lone crash, often the company's own news. That weakens the case.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: Your parabolic long reached the 9 EMA on day two and you sold what the plan called for. The rest has sat in a tight range for two weeks.
choices: A new setup, a new trade, its own stop
Hold; the 9 EMA was never the exit
Sell; a snap back is never held longer
questions.answer: A new setup, a new trade, its own stop
questions.why: Hold longer only if a new setup forms, a tight range or a Wedge Pop. Then it is a new trade with its own stop and plan. Bracco: a fast bounce, or a tight range for weeks.
questions.lesson_line: The bounce is one trade. The range after it is another, with its own stop.

wrong.Hold; the 9 EMA was never the exit: The 9 EMA is where the parabolic trade is done. Anything after is a new plan.
wrong.Sell; a snap back is never held longer: It can be held, as a new trade. Bracco kept SOXL as a swing after it worked.

questions.q: If the stock opens above a trim level, the trim must be taken at the open.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open. Do not wait for a better price.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through a trim level is the trim. Take it at the open.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: A $7 stock is down 55% in three days with all five boxes and a VWAP reclaim. It trades about $6 million a day.
choices: No; under $10 and $20 million a day
Yes; the burst is textbook
Yes, half size to respect the spread
Yes; small caps are where it is common
questions.answer: No; under $10 and $20 million a day
questions.why: No. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. Bracco notes the setup is common in small caps and prefers mid to large caps.
questions.lesson_line: A textbook burst in a thin stock is still a thin stock.

wrong.Yes; the burst is textbook: The burst is fine and the stock is not ours. Liquidity comes first.
wrong.Yes, half size to respect the spread: Size does not make a thin stock liquid.
wrong.Yes; small caps are where it is common: Common is not the same as tradable. Bracco prefers mid to large caps.

questions.q: Which vehicles does our card prefer for this setup?
choices: Mid and large caps, plus ETFs
Small caps trading under $10
Stocks with no listed options
Only the broad index ETF itself
questions.answer: Mid and large caps, plus ETFs
questions.why: Mid and large caps and broad or sector ETFs. Bracco prefers mid to large caps, and ETFs are fine with no extra rules.
questions.lesson_line: Trade the panic in something you can get out of.

wrong.Small caps trading under $10: Under $10 fails the liquidity rule. Bracco prefers the bigger names.
wrong.Stocks with no listed options: Options are not the point. Size and volume are.
wrong.Only the broad index ETF itself: The index version is one of two contexts. Stocks and sector ETFs qualify too.

questions.q: What is the read?
questions.story: On one day six China names print the same climax: gap downs, heavy volume, all five boxes. Each reclaims VWAP before noon.
choices: The best setting; a group unwind
Pass; too many names is a crash
Take one; the others are copies
Wait a week for a retest to form
questions.answer: The best setting; a group unwind
questions.why: The best setting. A crowded group unwinding all at once is where this setup works best. HTHT fired with six names that day and reached 3R the next session.
questions.lesson_line: When a whole crowd gets out at once, the turn is a group event.

wrong.Pass; too many names is a crash: A group liquidation is forced selling, the kind that snaps back. A crash is the index, from a top.
wrong.Take one; the others are copies: Each name is its own trade with its own stop. Position count is a separate rule.
wrong.Wait a week for a retest to form: The buy is the reclaim, on the climax day. A week later the bounce is done.

questions.q: A parabolic long up 2R may be held through tomorrow's earnings report.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. We hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R. At 2R the gap risk is bigger than the cushion.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings is a gap you cannot stop. Five R buys the ticket; 2R does not.

questions.q: Account 40,000. Risk 0.5%. Fill 76.76, stop 73.20. How many shares?
questions.why: 56. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. A 4.6% stop means fewer shares, not a tighter stop.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size. Never the other way round.

questions.q: Is it a parabolic long candidate?
questions.story: Over three weeks a stock drifts from 60 to 48 in small, overlapping bars: a down day or two, then a bounce. Volume stays flat. Today it closes at the low.
choices: No; an orderly, overlapping decline
Yes; it is 20% down
Yes, if tomorrow gaps down
questions.answer: No; an orderly, overlapping decline
questions.why: No. An orderly, overlapping decline is not this setup; the fall has to accelerate with little bar overlap. Bracco passed on a market that was not parabolic.
questions.lesson_line: Twenty percent down slowly is a grind. The setup needs a burst.

wrong.Yes; it is 20% down: Percent alone is Bracco's named mistake. The structure is a stair-step.
wrong.Yes, if tomorrow gaps down: A gap into a grind is one box out of five. The burst is still missing.

questions.q: What is the lesson?
questions.story: You bought a Friday turn at 25.58, stop 24.94. Monday closed 24.49, through the stop. The low came Thursday at 23.85, and by Friday the stock sat at the 9 EMA.
choices: A new low: selling was not done
Hold on; it reached the 9 EMA
Widen the stop to the Monday low
Buy more at Monday's close
questions.answer: A new low: selling was not done
questions.why: A new low under the climax low means the selling was not done, and the stop is the exit. The next turn, not the Friday turn, was the trade.
questions.lesson_line: The first turn is often a day early. The stop costs one R; the next turn is a new trade.

wrong.Hold on; it reached the 9 EMA: It got there from a lower low. Holding through the stop is how one R becomes five.
wrong.Widen the stop to the Monday low: The stop only moves up. Never wider.
wrong.Buy more at Monday's close: Never add when down. A re-entry needs a new trigger, as a new trade.

questions.q: 3x ETFs are the preferred vehicles for the index version, with no extra rules.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. 3x ETFs are preferred and carry no extra rules.
questions.lesson_line: For the index turn, the 3x ETF is the tool, not the exception.

questions.q: The ETF trades 500,000 shares a day on average. Our ceiling on the position?
choices: 5,000 shares, 1% of daily volume
50,000 shares, a tenth of volume
No ceiling on an ETF this size
500 shares, a tenth of the cap
questions.answer: 5,000 shares, 1% of daily volume
questions.why: 5,000 shares. Never own more than 1% of the average daily volume, and 1% of 500,000 is 5,000.
questions.lesson_line: One percent of the daily volume. In a panic, getting out is the whole game.

wrong.50,000 shares, a tenth of volume: A tenth of the day's volume. You could not get out of a panic in that size.
wrong.No ceiling on an ETF this size: An ETF with thin volume is as thin as any stock. The 1% rule stands.
wrong.500 shares, a tenth of the cap: A tenth of the ceiling. The rule is 1%.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought at 52.00 with the stop at 50.90. Next morning it opens 49.50. The first 30-minute bar's low is 48.70.
choices: Out; that low is past the 2R cap
48.70 is the new stop; hold on
Hold and wait for the close
Sell half at the open, hold half
questions.answer: Out; that low is past the 2R cap
questions.why: Out. The first 30 minutes decide, with a ceiling: 48.70 is a 3R loss, past 2R, so you get out.
questions.lesson_line: The gap rule has a ceiling. Past 2R in the first 30 minutes, you are done.

wrong.48.70 is the new stop; hold on: The 30-minute low is the new stop only inside 2R. A 3R loss is past the ceiling.
wrong.Hold and wait for the close: The decision is the first 30 minutes, not the close.
wrong.Sell half at the open, hold half: The rule is all or nothing after the first 30 minutes. Half is a guess.

questions.q: For the blow-off unwind, what came before the fall?
choices: A 50%+ run in days or weeks
A quiet base near highs
A slow downtrend of months
An earnings gap, then a fade
questions.answer: A 50%+ run in days or weeks
questions.why: A parabolic run of 50% or more in days or weeks: the stock was a parabolic-short candidate. Kullamagi's premise is a successful parabolic short that then crashed.
questions.lesson_line: The unwind needs a blow-off before it. No run, no rubber band.

wrong.A quiet base near highs: A base before a fall is a breakdown. The unwind needs a vertical run first.
wrong.A slow downtrend of months: That is the other context, the capitulation in a decline, measured in ATRs.
wrong.An earnings gap, then a fade: A gap is one day. The run is the whole parabolic move.

questions.q: Which setup is it?
questions.story: A stock has three straight up days and two gap-up opens, each day a bigger gain than the last. Today it gaps up again, then breaks under VWAP by 10:30.
choices: A parabolic short; the burst ran up
A parabolic long; the gap is the climax
A flat base breakout
questions.answer: A parabolic short; the burst ran up
questions.why: A parabolic short. The burst runs up and the climax gaps up, shorted as it breaks under VWAP with the stop over the high. The long is the same five boxes mirrored.
questions.lesson_line: Which way did it gap. Up is the short, down is the long.

wrong.A parabolic long; the gap is the climax: The long's climax gaps down. This one gapped up after three up days.
wrong.A flat base breakout: There is no base. Three vertical days and a gap is a burst.

questions.q: Which card?
questions.story: A leader fresh out of a base drops 2 ATR in one afternoon into its old high. The volume is the day's heaviest, then it turns. Yesterday it closed at a high.
choices: Mean Reversion form A; a one-day flush
A parabolic long; it dropped 2 ATR
A U&R at the old high
questions.answer: Mean Reversion form A; a one-day flush
questions.why: Mean Reversion form A. Bracco's one-day flush in a leader into a level is that card. A parabolic long needs 3 to 5 straight down days with two gap downs.
questions.lesson_line: Count the down days. One day in a leader is Mean Reversion; three to five is parabolic.

wrong.A parabolic long; it dropped 2 ATR: One afternoon is not a burst. The burst is three to five sessions.
wrong.A U&R at the old high: The level matters, but the 2 ATR flush on heavy volume names the Mean Reversion card.

questions.q: Which family?
questions.story: A stock is 20% under its 200-day after a four-day, 60% fall with two gap downs. It undercuts no visible level; it only reclaims VWAP after the low.
choices: Parabolic; a U&R needs a level
A U&R; VWAP is the level
A flat base; wait for the pivot
questions.answer: Parabolic; a U&R needs a level
questions.why: The parabolic family. A U&R undercuts a visible low after a dip of a few percent, in a stock above its 200-day. A parabolic long needs no level and may sit under the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: No level, under the 200-day, after a crash: that is parabolic territory, not a U&R.

wrong.A U&R; VWAP is the level: VWAP is the trigger, not a level. A U&R needs a visible low and a stock above its 200-day.
wrong.A flat base; wait for the pivot: Nothing is basing. A four-day crash is a burst.

questions.q: Hidden ticker; the chart ends on a gap-down day. Does the fall show the five boxes? Take it or pass.
choices: Take it; five boxes, strong close
Pass; a stair-step, no burst
Pass; the climax day closed at its low
questions.answer: Take it; five boxes, strong close
questions.why: Take it. All five boxes, 43.4% off the high in 17 sessions. A 3.4% gap down on 3.6x volume, a close 2.2% off the open. The clearest V in our set; 3R the next session.
questions.lesson_line: Five boxes and a strong close on the gap-down day. That is the picture.

wrong.Pass; a stair-step, no burst: Look again: the last days are the steepest, with gaps. That is a burst.
wrong.Pass; the climax day closed at its low: The last bar closed 2.2% above its open. The V is there.

questions.q: Hidden ticker; the chart ends on a gap-down day whose volume ran 1.5 times its average. Take it or pass.
choices: Pass; the climax needs 2x volume
Take it; the boxes are ticked
Take it; the gap is enough
questions.answer: Pass; the climax needs 2x volume
questions.why: Pass. The climax day ends at 2 times its 50-day average volume or more; this one ran 1.5x. The volume climax was in the index that day, not in this name.
questions.lesson_line: The crowd has to be in this stock, not just in the index.

wrong.Take it; the boxes are ticked: Four boxes and a stretch were there. Volume is its own gate and it missed.
wrong.Take it; the gap is enough: The gap is box five. The climax volume is a separate rule.

questions.q: Bracco's best turns come on a Monday, after down days into the weekend.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Bracco's Monday Effect: notable capitulations and turns have come on a Monday. DB and GE in our examples were Monday climaxes.
questions.lesson_line: Bracco's best turns have come on Mondays. Do not buy the Friday before one.

questions.q: Fill 20.50. The climax low is 19.00 and the stop sits five cents under it. How far below the fill is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 7.56%. Between 3% and 8%, so size down by the formula; over 8% would be a skip. SLG's stop was 7.2% and it reached 3R in 6 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the honest stop before the size. Wide but under 8% is fewer shares, not no trade.

questions.q: What does the rulebook say?
questions.story: Ten trading days after the climax your parabolic long sits at 0.6R. The stop was never touched and the 9 EMA is still above.
choices: Sold; under 1R after 10 sessions
Hold; the stop was never hit
Add; it has proved the low is in
Move the stop up and wait a month
questions.answer: Sold; under 1R after 10 sessions
questions.why: Sold. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money. A snap back that has not snapped in ten days is not snapping.
questions.lesson_line: This bounce lives for days. Ten days under 1R and the money has a better home.

wrong.Hold; the stop was never hit: The stop is one exit. Time is the other. Bracco holds these one to three days.
wrong.Add; it has proved the low is in: Never add. A proved low with no bounce is a range, a different trade.
wrong.Move the stop up and wait a month: A month is a swing trade. This was a snap back and it did not snap.

questions.q: Most parabolic longs reach the 9 EMA, as Bracco's magnet claim says for the short.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The mirror is not true for longs. In our test only about 4 in 10 reached the 9 EMA before the day's low broke. Take the target when it is offered.
questions.lesson_line: The 9 EMA is the target, not a promise. Four in ten get there.

questions.q: After a three-day crash from 847 to 202 the 9 EMA sits above 260. What does our card warn?
choices: The 9 EMA can stay out of reach
The 9 EMA is reached within days
A bigger crash, a bigger bounce
Skip; the 9 EMA is too close
questions.answer: The 9 EMA can stay out of reach
questions.why: The 9 EMA can be out of reach. After a crash from far above, CAR's 9 EMA was not reached for weeks. Expecting it every time is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Room to the target is good. A target in another zip code is a warning.

wrong.The 9 EMA is reached within days: After a crash from far above, it can take weeks. CAR is the case.
wrong.A bigger crash, a bigger bounce: A bigger crash means a farther 9 EMA. Bounce size is not the rule.
wrong.Skip; the 9 EMA is too close: The problem is the opposite. The 9 EMA is far, not close.

questions.q: What decides?
questions.story: On one Friday 83 names print the climax: every box ticked, every context met, heavy volume. It is the first week of a slide from an all-time high.
choices: The market reading, not the bars
The box count; five beats four
The volume; the heaviest day wins
Nothing; take all 83 of them
questions.answer: The market reading, not the bars
questions.why: The market reading. All 83 were stopped and none reached 5R; the real low came 16 sessions later. The rule reads the climax; the reading has to say whether the selling is done.
questions.lesson_line: Perfect bars in the first week of a crash are still the first week of a crash.

wrong.The box count; five beats four: Every one of the 83 had every box. The count could not separate them.
wrong.The volume; the heaviest day wins: Volume was heavy across the board. The date decided, not the volume.
wrong.Nothing; take all 83 of them: Taking all of them lost all of them. Context is a gate.

questions.q: What is the lesson?
questions.story: A 44% fall to 8.2 ATR under the 50-day, four boxes, 4.4x volume, a green close. Bought at 23.10, stop 21.70; stopped out the next day. Six sessions later, in the same panic, a different stock turned and ran.
choices: The first turn is often early
Never buy a bank in a panic
Widen the stop on the next buy
Heavy volume was the warning
questions.answer: The first turn is often early
questions.why: The first turn after a shock often comes too early. The panic had one more leg; the stop kept the cost to one R and the next trigger was a new trade.
questions.lesson_line: Being early is a recipe for disaster. The stop is the cure.

wrong.Never buy a bank in a panic: The sector was not the problem. The timing inside the panic was.
wrong.Widen the stop on the next buy: A wider stop would have paid more for the same wrong day. The stop only moves up.
wrong.Heavy volume was the warning: Heavy volume is part of the setup, not a warning. The shock had one more leg, that is all.

questions.q: Buy again?
questions.story: You were stopped out of a parabolic long on Tuesday. Thursday the same stock prints a new low, turns, and reclaims VWAP again, with the burst boxes still ticked.
choices: Yes; a new trade with its own stop
No; one try per climax
Yes, with a wider stop this time
No; wait for the 9 EMA
questions.answer: Yes; a new trade with its own stop
questions.why: Yes. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule. At most three tries in a week.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a verdict on the setup. The next reclaim is a new trade.

wrong.No; one try per climax: The limit is 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month, not one.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop this time: The stop is the day's low again. A wider stop to avoid a repeat is the mistake.
wrong.No; wait for the 9 EMA: The 9 EMA is the target, not the trigger. The trigger is the reclaim.

questions.q: The run's low was 20.00 and the peak 34.00. The run before the unwind, in percent?
questions.why: 70%. The peak over the run's low, minus one. The blow-off unwind wants a prior run of 50% or more in days or weeks; Kullamagi's successful parabolic short.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the run before the fall. The rubber band needs the stretch first.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: A 3x inverse Nasdaq ETF is 35% off its high with all five boxes ticked. The index is rallying to new highs.
choices: No; its climax is the index topping
Yes; five boxes is five boxes
Yes; inverse funds snap back harder
questions.answer: No; its climax is the index topping
questions.why: No. An inverse fund's selling climax is simply the index making a high. A bounce there is a bet on an index pullback, a different setup. SQQQ with all five boxes made nothing.
questions.lesson_line: An inverse fund does not capitulate. The index does, and this is its mirror image.

wrong.Yes; five boxes is five boxes: The boxes describe a stock's panic. Here they describe the index's strength.
wrong.Yes; inverse funds snap back harder: They snap back only if the index pulls back. That is a different trade with different odds.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, target.
questions.story: BABA, 2022-03-15: 43% off the high in 17 sessions, all five boxes, a 3.4% gap down on 3.6x volume. Late morning it reclaims VWAP after the low.
choices: Market at reclaim; stop under low; 9 EMA
Limit far below; wide stop; hold a month
Buy the open; stop under the 200-day
questions.answer: Market at reclaim; stop under low; 9 EMA
questions.why: Market order at the reclaim, stop a few cents under the climax low, target the daily 9 EMA. On our bars BABA closed 2.2% above its open and reached 3R the next session.
questions.lesson_line: Entry at the reclaim, stop under the low, target the 9 EMA. Write it before the turn.

wrong.Limit far below; wide stop; hold a month: A limit far under the low never fills on the turn, and a month is not this trade.
wrong.Buy the open; stop under the 200-day: The open is before the turn, and the 200-day is nowhere near the stop.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: Monday. The index gaps down more than an ATR, four ATR under its 50-day; the VIX jumps to 31. A liquid ETF prints all five boxes on 3x volume and reclaims VWAP at 10:40.
choices: Take it; the index is capitulating too
Pass; a VIX over 30 means more downside
Pass; a Monday gap is a trap
questions.answer: Take it; the index is capitulating too
questions.why: Take it. The index capitulating too, a gap down of an ATR or more, a Monday, a fast VIX move into 30. That is the best context and Bracco's own cue list for an index turn.
questions.lesson_line: A Monday gap with the VIX spiking and the index stretched: that is the day.

wrong.Pass; a VIX over 30 means more downside: A fast move into 30 is Bracco's cue to look for the turn, not to run from it.
wrong.Pass; a Monday gap is a trap: The Monday gap is the climax. Bracco's best turns have come on Mondays.

questions.q: The Model Book's old Parabolic Long card says ride a stock up its vertical run. What is our parabolic long?
choices: The burst mirrored: crash, then turn
The same; ride the run bar by bar
A short at the top of the run
questions.answer: The burst mirrored: crash, then turn
questions.why: The mirror of Bracco's burst: a burst down, then the turn. Our rulebook makes the long the mirror image; the old card describes the opposite trade and is overruled.
questions.lesson_line: Our parabolic long buys the crash's end, not the run's middle.

wrong.The same; ride the run bar by bar: That is the overruled card. Riding the run is the parabolic short's setup, from the other side.
wrong.A short at the top of the run: That is the parabolic short. The long is its mirror, after the fall.

questions.q: Entry 40.00, stop 38.50, the 9 EMA at 45.10. Which comes first on the way up, 3R or the 9 EMA?
choices: 3R at 44.50, before the 9 EMA
The 9 EMA, before 3R
They are the same level
questions.answer: 3R at 44.50, before the 9 EMA
questions.why: 3R first. One R is the fill minus the stop; three of those above the fill is 44.50, under the 9 EMA at 45.10. Know both levels before the open.
questions.lesson_line: Mark 3R and the 9 EMA before the open. Whichever comes first, you have a plan for it.

wrong.The 9 EMA, before 3R: The 9 EMA is 45.10 and 3R is 44.50. Do the arithmetic.
wrong.They are the same level: Close, not the same. Do the arithmetic before the open.

questions.q: What happened next, and why?
questions.story: All five boxes, a close at the top of the range, 7.4% off the open. The index has just lost its 200-day for the first time in a year. A perfect-looking V.
choices: A new low next day; a fresh breakdown
3R the next session; a textbook V
Flat for a month; no edge either way
questions.answer: A new low next day; a fresh breakdown
questions.why: A new low the next day. A perfect-looking V in a fresh breakdown is the worst setting; NBIS fell 12.2% the next session. The first days of a breakdown are not this setup.
questions.lesson_line: A V on the first leg of a breakdown is a trap with a nice shape.

wrong.3R the next session; a textbook V: The shape was textbook. The place in the move was the first leg down.
wrong.Flat for a month; no edge either way: Fresh breakdowns do not go flat. They go lower.

questions.q: On Bracco's line, which burst is stronger?
questions.story: Two stocks print a climax day with the same volume and the same context. One ticks all five boxes. The other is one box short.
choices: The burst with all five boxes
The burst one box short
Equal; the box count adds nothing
questions.answer: The burst with all five boxes
questions.why: The all-five burst. Bracco's line: not every box needs to be satisfied, but the more boxes checked, the stronger the setup.
questions.lesson_line: More boxes ticked reads stronger, on Bracco's line. Not every box is needed.

wrong.The burst one box short: One box fewer is a weaker read on Bracco's line, not a stronger one.
